title: OpenAPI Scanner — OpenAPIScanner.scan() / derive_module_id()
description: Byte-equivalent OpenAPIScanner behaviour across Python / TypeScript / Rust SDKs. `expected.modules` entries are compared structurally (parsed-JSON deep equality), not as raw strings.

Minimal GET /users → one module, users.get

test_cases.description: With no hooks installed, output is identical to the corresponding hook-free case

operationId normalisation pins the two word-boundary regexes on acronyms (getHTTPResponse, getUserID, OAuth2Token, getIDs), digits (v2Items) and hyphens (list-pets); a FastAPI-style ID that is already legal passes through unchanged, __ runs included; a trailing '_' is stripped from the operationId branch only; an astral character is ONE code point and becomes ONE '_' (JavaScript needs the u flag). getIDs -> get_i_ds is a known limitation, pinned so that every SDK produces it
Path-derived IDs are normalised like operationIds: hyphens and camelCase path segments become snake_case, and a segment's leading/trailing underscores are stripped
A segment that still begins with a digit after normalisation is not repaired (that would invent a name): the module is emitted with a warning, from both the path branch and the operationId branch

warnings: module_id 'v1.2fa.post' is not a legal apcore module ID: segment '2fa' must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; name this operation with a derive_module_id or transform_module hook
module_id '3ds' is not a legal apcore module ID: segment '3ds' must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; name this operation with a derive_module_id or transform_module hook

test_cases.description: base_path_prefix is part of the final module_id and is normalised with it: Pet-Store -> pet_store
A derive_module_id hook's return value is normalised like the default derivation: Custom-Space.GetThing -> custom_space.get_thing
The legality check runs after deduplicate_ids, so a renamed module's warning names the ID actually emitted (3ds_2) and follows the dedup warning

warnings: module_id '3ds' is not a legal apcore module ID: segment '3ds' must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; name this operation with a derive_module_id or transform_module hook
Module ID renamed from '3ds' to '3ds_2' to avoid collision
module_id '3ds_2' is not a legal apcore module ID: segment '3ds_2' must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; name this operation with a derive_module_id or transform_module hook

test_cases.description: Path segments are normalised one by one and dropped when empty; a path with no surviving segment falls back to root.<method>, exactly like GET /

The final normalisation returns a legal ID unchanged: a derive_module_id hook returning abc_ under base_path_prefix pre_ is emitted as pre_.abc_ - no trailing '_' is stripped, per segment or at the end. Drivers implement the named hook always_returns_legal_trailing_underscore_id

Each character outside the alphabet becomes its own '_' (list--pets -> list__pets, never collapsed); a path segment keeps its trailing '_' (GET /items_ -> items_.get); and lowercasing runs after the replacement, so U+212A KELVIN SIGN becomes '_' and is stripped (Kelvin -> elvin), never 'k'
